subject: Post-call: Dedicated pool design, isolation requirements, and SLA confirmation
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.inference>
To: Eva Martin <eva.martin@orchidtx.com>, Julio Ramos <jramos@orchidtx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated pool design, isolation requirements, and SLA confirmation

Thanks for the time earlier today — quick recap and agreed next steps so we have alignment before I loop in procurement and engineering.

Key pain & goals you shared
- Data isolation: production model inputs are PHI-adjacent and need tenant isolation and customer-managed keys.
- Predictable latency: live inference for clinician-facing UI requires p95 under 200ms for 1k token spans.
- Cost predictability: Orchid needs committed pricing tied to reserved capacity with defined burst behavior.

What we propose (high level)
- Dedicated reserved pool: baseline of 4x A100-equivalent slots for primary capacity, autoscale up to 12 for bursts.
- Isolation: single-tenant VPC with encrypted KV cache, optional on-prem connector for audit-only datasets. KMS/HSM integration available.
- SLA targets: 99.9% uptime on Dedicated, p95 latency target 120–180ms (depends on model and batch settings), with fallback to lower-cost variants on incident.

Actions we agreed
1) I will share a short SOW draft and a pool schematic for your security and procurement review — attached. (Olga) — by EOD today.
2) Orchid to share a short list of production models, average request length, and expected qps during peak hours (Eva) — by Tue 6/16.
3) Marissa to scope isolation runbook and ops playbook items (Marissa) — draft by Wed 6/17.
4) Aditya to prepare a pricing sketch for 12-month reserved commitment + burst rates (Aditya) — preliminary numbers by Thu 6/18.

Open clarifying notes
- Julio noted SOC 2 evidence and specific audit logs are required; I’ve flagged that to our security team. We can include sample retention settings in the runbook.
- We recommended a small canary period (2 weeks) to validate perf at production load before full cutover.

If that matches your read, please reply with any edits and we’ll move the draft SOW to procurement.

Thanks,
Olga

- Data residency: all inference calls must route through our US region only.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II report and sample audit logs required for vendor security sign-off.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Adding a few technical clarifications from the infra perspective — forwarding small ops checklist below.

Marissa's ops checklist (short):
- Isolation: confirm whether Orchid prefers network-level isolation only or full compute silo per model family. Recommendation: compute silo per prod workload for PHI-adjacent traffic.
- KV Cache: customer-encrypted KV cache with retention 30 days; option to purge on request.
- Autoscale policy: scale targets based on p95 latency > 150ms for 3 consecutive 1-min windows; warmup concurrency pre-scale to avoid cold-starts.
- Canary tests: synthetic load at 120% expected peak qps for 2 hours; verify p95 < 180ms and no error-rate delta > 0.1%.
- Incident response: automatic fallback to quantized model variant (lower cost/higher latency) + alert to Orchid on-call.

I’ll attach a short runbook draft to the HubSpot record and share the link shortly. If Orchid confirms compute-silo preference, we’ll update the SOW wording to include per-silo provisioning and isolation pricing.

-Marissa
